title: URLs and requests
summary: Take a URL apart, then read an HTTP request as the server sees it.

steps.title: Anatomy of a URL
body: scheme  user     host     port   path          query     fragment
- **scheme** picks the protocol and the default port (http 80, https 443).
- **host** is looked up in DNS. **path** and **query** are sent to the server.
- the **fragment** (`#reviews`) is *never sent*: it's for the browser only.
- characters outside the safe set are **percent-encoded**: a space is `%20`.

steps.prompt: Which part of `https://shop.example/search?q=red%20shoes#results` does the server **not** receive?
options: the host name (it's in the `Host` header)
steps.explain: Fragments stay in the browser. The host travels in the `Host` header (and in TLS SNI).

steps.title: Parse a URL
prompt: Write `(string Scheme, string Host, int Port, string Path, string Query)` `ParseUrl(string url)` without using `Uri`.
- path defaults to `/`; query is the text after `?` without it (or `""`)
starter: (string Scheme, string Host, int Port, string Path, string Query) ParseUrl(string url)
solution: (string Scheme, string Host, int Port, string Path, string Query) ParseUrl(string url)
hints: Strip the fragment first, then split off the scheme at `://`.
Then cut the query at `?`, then split authority from path at the first `/`.

steps.title: A request is just text
body: HTTP/1.1 is a text protocol. After the TCP (and TLS) connection, the client sends:
- **headers**: `Name: value`, one per line, names case-insensitive.
- an **empty line**, then the optional **body**. Lines end in `\r\n`.
`Host` is mandatory in HTTP/1.1: one IP can serve many sites, and this is how the server knows which.

steps.prompt: Is the method **safe** (doesn't change server state) and so fine to retry/cache?
steps.explain: PUT and DELETE are not safe but are **idempotent**: doing them twice has the same effect as once. POST is neither.

steps.prompt: Complete this raw request so it fetches `https://shop.example/health`.
steps.explain: The method starts the request line; `Host` names the site.

steps.title: Parse a request
prompt: Write `(string Method, string Path, Dictionary<string, string> Headers, string Body) ParseRequest(string raw)`.
- lines are separated by `\r\n`; the first is the request line (`METHOD target VERSION`). Return the target **without** its query string as `Path`.
- header lines until the first empty line: split at the **first** `:` and trim the value. The dictionary must be case-insensitive.
- everything after the empty line is the body (`""` if none).
starter: (string Method, string Path, Dictionary<string, string> Headers, string Body) ParseRequest(string raw)
solution: (string Method, string Path, Dictionary<string, string> Headers, string Body) ParseRequest(string raw)
template:
var dojoR = ParseRequest("POST /api/orders?src=web HTTP/1.1
Host: shop.example
Content-Type: application/json
X-Time: 10:30

{"qty":2}");
hints: Split head and body at the first `\r\n\r\n`.
For headers use `IndexOf(':')` (the first one) so `10:30` survives.
